title: Enablement Lab Playbook: Model Rollout & POC Facilitation
body:
Purpose:
This playbook is a lightweight facilitator’s guide for a 3‑hour customer Enablement Lab focused on rolling a model into a customer POC or pilot using Redwood Inference. It combines agenda, slide-outline skeleton, facilitator cues, and a short technical runbook so an SE team can run a fast, repeatable session that leaves the customer with an actionable deployment blueprint.

Audience:
- Solutions Engineers (lead facilitator)
- Customer technical leads / ML engineers
- Customer product manager or PMM
- Optional: SRE/infra from customer + Redwood SRE on call

Session goals (pick 2–3 primary before the session):
- Validate end‑to‑end latency/cost on realistic request traffic
- Confirm model variant (FP16/4-bit) compatibility with customer constraints
- Produce a step-by-step deployment checklist the customer can execute post-session
- Identify any unblockers (data access, networking, auth) and owners

Pre-reqs (to confirm 3 days before):
- Customer has provided sample traffic (JSONL) and a small evaluation prompt set (50–200 examples)
- Access: service account or API token with scoped access; VPN/VPC peering arranged if doing Private test
- Workspace: a shared docs folder (we use the POC template in Confluence) and a test dataset in S3/GCS or sample payloads in Drive
- SE checklist: local test harness, tracing-enabled client, and cost-estimate script

Logistics:
- Length: 3 hours (recommended); alternatives: 90min focused tech or half-day strategy + lab
- Room: dual screens (slides + live terminal), whiteboard for rollout map
- Roles: facilitator (SE), recording/notes (SE teammate), tech lead (customer), product sponsor (customer)

Agenda (90–180 minute adaptable):
- 0:00–0:10 Welcome + goals alignment (Facilitator)
  - Quick intros, confirm primary session goals, success criteria
  - Call out any must-fix constraints (data residency, latency SLOs)
- 0:10–0:30 Architecture walkthrough (Customer + SE)
  - Current infra, where inference will sit, network topology, security boundary
  - SE: map Redwood components to customer infra (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
- 0:30–0:55 Hands-on demo: baseline perf & smoke tests (SE lead)
  - Run a short smoke test: single-request latency; show token-level tracing
  - Run a small burst to show throughput characteristics
- 0:55–1:10 Slide break: deployment options & tradeoffs (SE)
  - Quick bullets: cost vs latency, autoscaling behavior, caching, quantization
- 1:10–1:45 Breakout: run customer sample traffic and tune (paired exercise)
  - Split into two pods: runtime tuning (batching/kv caching) and routing/cost profile
  - SEs jump in to help with config changes live
- 1:45–2:05 Deep-dive: security & compliance checklist (SE + Security SME)
  - KMS, audit logs, network egress, data masking patterns
- 2:05–2:30 Rollout plan and next steps (facilitated by SE & customer PM)
  - Ownership matrix, milestones, deliverables (e.g., pilot exec, success metrics)
- 2:30–2:45 Parking lot + open questions + action item recap

Slide outline (fast skeleton — keep slides punchy, 10–15 slides total):
1) Title + session goals (1 slide)
2) Agenda + roles (1 slide)
3) Customer infra snapshot (1 slide, customer-provided diagram)
4) Redwood serving options overview (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) (1 slide)
5) Sizing & cost tradeoffs (1 slide; quick numbers and sensitivity)
6) Latency/throughput demo results (2 slides: baseline and tuned)
7) Tuning knobs and recommended configs (1–2 slides: batching, caching, quantization)
8) Security & compliance considerations (1 slide)
9) Rollout blueprint + milestones (1 slide)
10) Risks & mitigations (1 slide)
11) Action items and owner assignment (1 slide)

Facilitation notes & cues (explicit, copyable prompts):
- When aligning goals: "Which of these outcomes would make this lab a win for your team?" (ask customer to pick 1–2)
- If the customer pushes back on time: offer to move strategy discussion to async follow-up and keep the session technical
- Live tuning: try 1 change at a time (e.g., batch size from 1→4). Capture before/after token cost and p95 latency.
- Use the whiteboard to draw a deployment flow: identify where KV cache sits and what is ephemeral vs persisted

Quick technical runbook (commands and artifacts to have ready):
- Smoke test harness: curl example (tokenized payload, trace header enabled)
- Perf script: python perf_runner.py --concurrency 8 --duration 60 --model <model-id>
- Cost script: estimate_cost.py --model <model> --tokens_per_request <n> --qps <m>
- Config snippet to flip on prefix/KV caching (example to paste into customer's config):
  - cache.enabled: true
  - cache.scope: request-prefix
  - cache.max_entries: 20000

Security / compliance quick hits to confirm:
- Is data routed through customer VPC? If not, red flag for regulated data
- Confirm KMS integration and audit log retention window
- Are any PII fields present in the sample payload? If yes, we should redact or obfuscate during lab runs

Success criteria (post-session deliverables):
- Executable 1–2 page rollout checklist shared with owners and dates
- Baseline and tuned perf numbers (p50/p95 latency, tokens per second, cost per 1M tokens)
- A short runbook (3–5 commands) that the customer can run to reproduce the smoke test
- Identified blockers with owners and target resolution dates

Common pitfalls and mitigation (learned from prior POCs):
- Pitfall: customer traffic sample is too synthetic -> mitigation: insist on 100+ real examples or instrumented recording
- Pitfall: permissions mismatch when testing Private -> mitigation: pre-validate service account prior to session
- Pitfall: We do tuning without clear SLO -> mitigation: set explicit latency/cost SLOs at the start

Post-session artifacts to deliver (SE owner identifies):
- Deck (trimmed to 8–10 slides) with annotated architecture and final config
- Rollout checklist (owner, step, script, validation step)
- Perf log file + short interpretation note (1 slide summary)

Follow-ups and escalation path:
- If a security blocker: open SE-Security Slack escalation and tag security SME; target 48h triage
- If infra gap (network, VPC): open JIRA with customer infra team, link to lab artifacts
- If model incompatibility (tensor format/ops): route to Applied ML for model onboarding ticket

Notes to self (facilitator quick reminders):
- Bring small sample tokens for local demo if customer network is flaky
- Record terminal commands in the shared doc as you run them
- Keep the session interactive; ask customers to drive config decisions so ownership is clear

Open questions to resolve after lab (examples):
- Will the customer accept a quantized variant for production? (technical + product approval required)
- What is the expected peak QPS multiplier for holiday/weekend events?

Template action items (copy/paste into meeting notes):
- Owner: <name> | Task: Provide full synthetic dataset or instrumented logs | Due: YYYY-MM-DD
- Owner: <name> | Task: Confirm KMS key and audit log retention policy | Due: YYYY-MM-DD
- Owner: <name> | Task: Run tuned perf script and upload logs to shared folder | Due: YYYY-MM-DD

Appendix (handy snippets):
- Perf runner minimal example (python)
  - import requests
  - for _ in range(n): requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)
- Simple curl smoke test
  - curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"hello world"}'

End of playbook — quick checklist before you close the session:
- Confirm action items and owners
- Reiterate success criteria and how we’ll measure them
- Schedule follow-up review (30–90 days depending on pilot length)

Parking lot (things to document after):
- Model variant comparison table (latency vs token cost)
- Example rollout scripts for k8s deployment or Terraform snippet for Dedicated

-- facilitator notes signed off by: Maya Chen (SE lead)
